subtopics.title: India-UAE partnership
subtopics.summary: India and the UAE agreed to double bilateral trade to over USD 200 billion by 2032. Their ties span energy, with a long-term LNG deal, civil nuclear cooperation and defence collaboration, along with a proposal for data embassies. The UAE also accounted for 18% of India's remittance flows.
facts: India and the UAE agreed to double bilateral trade to over USD 200 billion by 2032.
Bilateral trade was US$ 100 billion in FY 2024-25.
The UAE is India's 3rd largest trade partner, after China and the US.
In 2022, India became the first country with which the UAE signed a CEPA.
ADNOC Gas signed an agreement with HPCL to supply 0.5 million tonnes per annum of LNG for 10 years.
The UAE accounted for 18% of India's remittance flows.
India has access to the UAE's Al Dhafra Air Base for refuelling.
Both countries agreed to explore cooperation in small modular reactors and nuclear safety.
A proposal for offshore digital infrastructure would store critical national data as data embassies.

subtopics.title: UAE profile and the Kafala system
subtopics.summary: The UAE is a federal elective monarchy of seven emirates, with Abu Dhabi as its capital and the dirham as its currency. Under the Kafala system, an in-country sponsor, typically the employer, controls a migrant worker's visa and legal status. Workers cannot change jobs or leave the country without that sponsor's permission.
facts: The UAE is a federal elective monarchy composed of 7 emirates.
The UAE shares land borders with Oman and Saudi Arabia.
The UAE's maritime borders in the Persian Gulf are with Qatar and Iran.
The UAE's capital is Abu Dhabi and its currency is the dirham.
Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is the President; Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum is the Prime Minister.
Under Kafala, an in-country sponsor, typically the employer, controls a worker's visa and legal status.
Workers cannot change jobs or leave the country without the sponsor's permission.
Kafala can lead to exploitation, non-payment of wages, poor conditions and restricted movement.
Barakah is the Arab world's first nuclear power plant.
